ENKO Arou 001.notes:
Enkomi baked clay cylinder (##097, CM 1, 27 lines, 182 tokens, 47 legible groups including single-sign entries; excavated 1967, Schaeffer et al. 1968, 266–269; Valério 2016, 404–407, 420–424). Tripartite structure: Part I heading (.01), Part II entry-marked list (.02–.13) repeatedly using an X | Y-o-ti formula, and Part III continuous script (.13–.27) organized around recurring thematic stems (ta-la-ka, sa-ra-ni, sa-ri-jo-ti) with productive 069- (ja-) prefixing (.17, .27).

Thirty-six of 47 legible groups (31 of 42 multi-sign groups) read on the ruled grid. Twelve distinct multi-sign groups end in -023 (-ti), splitting into -po-ti (×3), -ro-ti (×3) and -jo-ti (×3), matching 1st-millennium Eteocypriot genitive/possessive -o-ti (Valério 2016, 398–400, 421–424). ENKO Atab 003.notes:
Enkomi baked clay tablet (##208, excavated 1953 by P. Dikaios; CM 2, 118 legible groups; Valério 2016, 447–448 Table II.2, 520–526). Entered on Valério's critical re-edition (text: 'emended'), which systematically restores 013 → 008 (na, ×12) and 064 → 065 (ni, ×5) across the tablet—separating CM 1 064 (o, 83% initial) from CM 2 065 (ni, 0% initial).

Exhibits three-stage agglutinative suffix chains (e-re → e-re-pi → e-re-pi-na; ta-ka → ta-ka-pi-na; and an unruled stem taking -ko and -na), the ka-pa-ni member of CM 2's four-case ka-pa-na/-ni/-sa/-ta paradigm, and on B.17 the adjacent pair ta-ra-wo₂ | a-sa-na matching Amathus Eteocypriot ICS 194 (ta-ra-wo, a-so-na) beside ENKO Atab 004 ta-ra-we₂ (ICS 193 ta-ra-wi). Faucounau's (1980, 384–386) Hurrian reading as a letter to the king of the Lukki fails against ruled 024=le, 075=ra, 051=pi and Valério's B.15 epigraphy.

RASH Atab 001.notes:
Small boustrophedon clay tablet (RS 17.06, ##212) excavated in 1953 in the private library of Rašap-abu at Ugarit (É. Masson 1974, 24–30; Valério 2016, 399, 540–543). Likely a letter: opening address with two consecutive -023 (-ti) words wrapped across boustrophedon line ends (A.01–02 and A.02–03), followed on A.03 by a group where the scribe erased a mistakenly carried-over -ti, and a two-word left-edge signature (B.lat.sin.).

Unlike RASH Atab 004 (RS 20.25), this tablet has no 051-028 (binu), yields zero decoy-calibrated Kinlaw 1967 or Monti 2017 matches at p <= 0.05 on the ruled grid, and shares two exact lexical parallels with Cyprus: 019-023 (u-ti) with ENKO Arou 001 (CM 1) and 006-025 (pa-ka) with ENKO Atab 002 (CM 2). The productive -o-ti / -ti ending points to an indigenous Cypriot / pre-Eteocypriot matrix grammar beside local Ugarit or Hurrian personal names (such as ka-se-ji), against Faucounau's Hurrian reading (1977, 235–236).

RASH Atab 004.notes:
A list of men, each named alone, with his father ('PN son of PN') or with his town ('PN, of GN'), as É. Masson read it (1974, 38) after Schaeffer's suggestion of a list of names (O. Masson 1969, 392 n. 22), closing with lines that name a minister and a scribe (B.17–19; É. Masson 1974, 34–35; Valério 2016, 356). Its names are those of Ugarit, Semitic with a Hurrian share, and its bn 'son' and its names in the genitive, ʾIlyāni of Siyannu among them, point to a Semitic language, as Valério concludes (2016, 395). Most identifications are those of Saporetti, Nahm, Faucounau and Valério, credited word by word, read here on one value for each sign.

Of 300 random groups of the same length drawn from the tablet's own signs and set against the syllabic names of the Akkadian texts of Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967), none fits as closely as Kôṯar-ʾabī or ʿAmmurapi, two as closely as ʾIlī-malik and six as ʾIlyānu; the value of 074 was chosen on ʿAmmurapi. Two Enkomi tablets, ENKO Atab 003 and 004, read on the same values, fit the same names in 10% and 3% of their legible groups of three signs or more, against 26% here. One legible group, in A.06, stays unread.

The tablet tells nothing of the languages Cypro-Minoan wrote on Cyprus (É. Masson 1974, 47).
